messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: high GPU pool saturation detected in us-west-2 (pool: rw-gpu-prod-12). Autoscaler attempted scale but hit quota/driver errors. @devin you're oncall — please ack and triage. :rotating_light:

devin (oncall-sre): acked. seeing a steep queue growth on inference-fanout for the past 6m. backlog -> 18k requests. autoscaler tried to add nodes at 5067891180 but failed with mixed errors. digging into node events now.

devin (oncall-sre): quick summary from metrics: GPU utilization plateaued ~92%, active_pods ~430 (limit 450), evictions spiked, and lots of cuda/xid and driver OOM entries in kernel logs. autoscaler returned: "quota exceeded" for new G4 nodes + some nodes flapped during join.

sara (sre-lead): tagging @ajay and @kai. If driver/kernel instability is reducing effective capacity we should consider draining affected pools and routing traffic to standby region. How wide is the Xid/OOM wave?

ajay (eng-runtime): we've got noisy Xid 31/77 repeating across 9 nodes. stack traces show nv_peer_to_peer and memory alloc spikes right before the Xid. suspect a large-model batch that triggers rare kernel path. Runtime logs: `kv_cache_size` jumps when requests hit model: redwood-llama-70b-quant.

kai (eng-infra): infra events: 3 nodes reported kernel oops and auto-reboot loop. Two join attempts failed with signature: `nvidia-driver: failing init, rc=-5`. quota limit for new GPUs in us-west-2 is at 0 autoscale attempts allowed until we request increase.

eve (cs-ops): cs update: a handful of customers on high-throughput plans reported elevated latency and timeouts on embeddings/generation. No PII leakage. Customers affected: org-147, org-202 (low impact but shopping cart queries slow). Will prepare a customer note if we need extended mitigation.

devin (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations I propose: 1) pause non-critical retrain/ingestion jobs to free headroom, 2) reduce max batch size for redwood-llama-70b-quant via runtime config to avoid the kernel path, 3) cordon + drain the 9 noisy nodes, 4) attempt soft-fallback: route some traffic to cpu-backed small models (latency hit) and us-east region. Opinions?

ajay (eng-runtime): +1 to decreasing batch size and runtime queue caps. I'll push a hot-config to lower batch_max_tokens and disable aggressive kv prefetch for redwood-llama-70b-quant. Patch below:

```yaml
model_profiles:
  redwood-llama-70b-quant:
    batch_max_tokens: 1024   # lowered from 4096
    kv_prefetch: false
    quant_sched: conservative
```

ajay (eng-runtime): this should reduce the memory blast that seems to trigger the Xid. Deploying to us-west-2 now (rolling, canary first).

kai (eng-infra): starting cordon/drain on nodes: gpu-node-uw2-192, gpu-node-uw2-197 ... using: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

devin (oncall-sre): running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending` shows 530 pending on us-west-2 after drain started. I'll start a targeted routing change on the ingress layer to send new sessions to us-east-1 for models above 4B.

sara (sre-lead): don't forget to update routing TTL and warn throttled customers. Also we should set an autoscale fallback policy to avoid repeated quota attempts causing churn.

ajay (eng-runtime): rolling canary of config done on 2 nodes -> no Xid observed in canary window (3m). I'll continue rollout. If stable, we can progressively uncordon nodes after driver patch.

kai (eng-infra): note: two kernel crash dump samples attached to node logs: `oops_ip: 0xffff... nvidia.ko+0x1b2f4`. I'll capture logs and open a ticket with driver vendor if we see replays after restart. For now we're avoiding full driver reloads on live nodes.

devin (oncall-sre): customer impact now: latency spike for ~6k requests, 120 5xxs observed, severity: S2-N1 for affected customers. Eve, please coordinate comms with ops.

eve (cs-ops): preparing an interim status message: "We're mitigating a GPU saturation issue causing higher latency in us-west-2. We've routed most heavy requests to us-east-1 and reduced memory pressure on models. Engineers are rolling a runtime config to avoid triggering driver bug. ETA next update: 20m." Want me to send?

sara (sre-lead): send now. Also, @ajay please add an eval check to prevent canary triggering the same kernel path. We should add a regression guard in Optimize.

ajay (eng-runtime): will add a regression test that runs a high-concurrency prefix through redwood-llama-70b-quant under quantized path.

kai (eng-infra): cordon/drain status: 6/9 drained, 2 nodes rebooted and rejoined cleanly after driver restart, 1 node failed join -> marking for manual repro and kernel-dug. I'll isolate it into the quarantine pool.

devin (oncall-sre): autoscaler: disabled proactive scale until driver investigation completes to avoid thrash (set autoscale.enabled=false for pool rw-gpu-prod-12). We're also temporarily raising concurrency limits in us-east to absorb load.

devin (oncall-sre): quick runbook snippet for oncall:
1) if Xid > 3 nodes in 10m, reduce batch_max_tokens and kv_prefetch for suspected models.
2) cordon/drain noisy nodes, route heavy traffic to standby region.
3) if driver reboots fail, quarantine node and gather crash dumps: `/var/crash/...`

sara (sre-lead): decision log: mitigations applied: runtime config lowered batch size, 6 nodes drained, autoscale temporarily disabled, heavy traffic routed to us-east-1, customer comms sent. Next: infra to reproduce on quarantined node and file vendor ticket; runtime to add regression test and consider a longer-term model-serving guardrail.

ajay (eng-runtime): observation: lowering batch size dropped memory spikes immediately and Xid events stopped on canaries. Full rollout in progress. Might be enough as a medium-term mitigation while infra pursues driver fix or model quantization rework.

kai (eng-infra): capturing crash dumps + dmesg, creating vendor ticket #DRV-12749. attaching node id and timestamps. Also requested emergency GPU quota bump with cloud provider (pending).

eve (cs-ops): customer comms: sent, and offered manual routing toggles for org-147 and org-202 while we stabilize. both accepted temporary reroute.

devin (oncall-sre): last check: queue down from 18k -> 2.1k in 22m, outstanding 5xxs dropping. rolling back autoscale hold only after vendor response or when Xid absent for 60m.

sara (sre-lead): thanks team. keep a 30m cadence updates in thread. I'll start an incident writeup once stable with root-cause hypothesis: model batch memory blowup hitting rare driver kernel path combined with autoscaler quota churn.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated (partial). Next update scheduled at 5067893660 or earlier.

devin (oncall-sre): marking this thread for postmortem. assigning action items: infra: reproduce & vendor ticket (#DRV-12749), runtime: regression test + guardrail, product: consider model serving defaults change, cs: follow-up comms.

sara (sre-lead): closing oncall shift handoff note: if any new escalation, wake me. otherwise I'll start the post-incident RCA draft. :white_check_mark:
